paper_metadata.title: Impact of Bilingualism on Cognitive Outcome After Stroke

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study utilized a large, consecutive stroke registry with clearly defined inclusion/exclusion criteria and a well-described baseline population. While it is a hospital-based sample, the recruitment process was systematic.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The patients were participants in the Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences stroke registry, initiated to study clinical profile and outcome in consecutive cases of acute stroke.
items.reasoning: The source is a specific institutional registry in Hyderabad, India, covering consecutive acute stroke cases.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Records of patients evaluated during 2006 to 2013 were reviewed. Patients with ischemic stroke >18 years and evaluated 3 to 24 months after stroke were included.
items.reasoning: The recruitment period and the use of a registry for identification are clearly stated.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Patients with ischemic stroke >18 years and evaluated 3 to 24 months after stroke were included. Patients with disabling stroke (modified Rankin Scale score>4), severe comorbidities, inadequate data, and preexisting dementia were excluded.
items.reasoning: Both inclusion and exclusion criteria are explicitly listed, including the 'zero time' (3-24 months post-stroke).

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Bilingualism is clearly defined and measured consistently across the sample. Although it relies on self-report/interview, this is standard for the field, and the study notes the lack of confounding by immigration.

items.evidence_snippet: Bilingualism was defined as the ability to communicate in 2 or more languages in interaction with other speakers of these same languages.
items.reasoning: A functional definition of the prognostic factor is provided.

items.reasoning: While the study mentions systematic study, it does not detail the specific tool or scale used to verify proficiency levels, relying likely on clinical interview.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Outcomes were measured using validated, standardized tools (ACE-R, NINDS-AIREN) by trained professionals. The use of age and education-matched norms for cognitive impairment reduces measurement bias.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: VaD was diagnosed as fulfilling National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke and Association Internationale pour la Recherche et l'Enseignement en Neurosciences (NINDS-AIREN) criteria... Vascular mild cognitive impairment was diagnosed in subjects with impairment in at least 1 cognitive domain subscore of ACE-R
items.reasoning: Standardized clinical criteria and psychometric cut-offs were used to define outcomes.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Cognitive evaluation was done using Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination–Revised (ACE-R)... adapted for Telugu- and Hindi-speaking populations... ACE-R has been validated in large studies of stroke outcome.
items.reasoning: The study used a validated and culturally adapted version of a recognized cognitive tool.

items.evidence_snippet: To study whether bilingualism was independently associated with poststroke cognitive impairment, we performed a series of logistic regressions.
items.reasoning: Multivariable logistic regression was used to adjust for age, education, occupation, and risk factors.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical approach was sound, using logistic regression and Bonferroni corrections for multiple testing. Results are reported transparently with Odds Ratios and Confidence Intervals.

items.reasoning: A logical, stepwise approach to model building was employed.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: The presence of cognitive impairment was the fixed factor for the logistic regression.
